function.name: calculate_tax
function.description: Computes the tax amount based on the taxable income and applicable tax brackets. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

taxable_income.description: The total income subject to tax, in dollars. This is a float type value.

tax_brackets.description: A list of tax brackets. Each bracket is a dict containing the upper limit and corresponding tax rate.

filing_status.description: The tax filing status of the individual.

state.description: The state for which the tax is being calculated. This should be in the two-letter state code format, such as 'CA' for California.

• 12 % up to $44 725
• 22 % up to $95 375
• **24 %** up to $182 250 | **24 %** | | **Married Filing Jointly** | • 10 % up to $22 050
• 12 % up to $89 450
• 22 % up to $190 750
• 24 % up to $364 200 | **12 %** | > **Answer:** > - **Single filer:** 24 % marginal rate > - **Married filing jointly:** 12 % marginal rate --- ### 2️⃣ How does the tax rate change if the filing status switches from **single** to **married filing jointly**? When you file jointly, your combined income is compared against *joint* thresholds, which are roughly twice the single thresholds. Because of this, the same $100 000 sits in a lower bracket when filing jointly. #### Example Calculation (using 2023 brackets) | Filing Status | Standard Deduction (2023) | Adjusted Gross Income after Deduction | Tax Owed (approx.) | Effective Tax Rate | |---------------|--------------------------|---------------------------------------|--------------------|---------------------| | **Single** | $13 850 | $86 150 | ≈ $16 500 | ≈ 19 % | | **Married Filing Jointly** | $27 700 | $72 300 | ≈ $9 800 | ≈ 14 % | > **Key Takeaway:** > - **Marginal rate drops** from 24 % (single) to 12 % (MFJ). > - **Effective rate** (total tax ÷ gross income) also tends to drop because of the larger standard deduction and the fact that many taxpayers fall into lower brackets when incomes are pooled. --- ### Quick Summary | Scenario | Marginal Rate | Approximate Effective Rate | |----------|--------------|----------------------------| | Single, $100 k taxable | 24 % | ~19 % | | Married Filing Jointly, $100 k taxable | 12 % | ~14 % | If you’d like me to crunch the exact numbers for a specific year or include additional factors (like itemized deductions, credits, etc.), just let me know!
